desc: Ideation: reduce to letter map `f`, derive `answer = changed + #cycles(len≥2) whose nodes all have in-degree exactly 1`, and the `-1` conditions (inconsistent map; or `len(dom)==26` with injective `f` and `changed>0`)
Refute the naive "+1 per cycle" formula via counterexample `S="abc", T="baa"` (answer 3, not 4)
Implement the final solution (parse, consistency check, `changed`, in-degree, isolated-cycle count, `-1` cases, output)

Verify achievability/lower-bound argument in detail: intra-group pre-merges are free at time 0 (so a free letter always exists when `|dom|<26` or `f` non-injective, and such a letter is never on an isolated cycle), dependency graph of dumps is acyclic except on isolated cycles, each costing exactly +1 with a reusable temporary letter

Final review of edge cases (N=1, `S==T` checked before the permutation `-1` test, `f(c)` outside `dom` as sink, self-loops as length-1 cycles, in-degree counted only over `dom`) and performance O(N + 26) with byte-level parsing
